h1:
Where to Stay in Sukhothai?
10 Hotels We've Reviewed
Prices Compared Across 3 Sites
heroSub: Ten Sukhothai hotels across every budget — a luxury rice-field resort in the Old Town, down to garden bungalows and guesthouses by the Yom River in the New Town. Covering the two main areas: the Old Town (next to the Historical Park) and the New Town. Starting from around ฿500–6,800/night.
introH2: 🏛️ Why does choosing the right area in Sukhothai matter?
introHtml: Sukhothai splits into two areas that feel distinctly different. The Old Town is the zone around the Sukhothai Historical Park — most stays here are garden resorts and boutiques, and you can cycle to the ancient ruins straight from your hotel. It's quiet and restful but has few dinner options at night. The New Town sits about 12 km away by the Yom River — a district of guesthouses and value hotels, within walking distance of markets, restaurants and the songthaew stop into the park. Many travellers book without checking which area they're in, then spend every day shuttling to and from the park. This guide brings together 10 Sukhothai hotels we've reviewed across every tier. Every pick has its own full review on our site, summarised from real guest reviews, with prices compared across 3 sites and direct booking links throughout.
mrtHtml: Sukhothai has no metro and the city is compact — you'll mostly use cars, motorbikes, bicycles or songthaews. From Sukhothai Airport into the Old Town is about 40 minutes. The main areas in this guide: Old Town — around the Sukhothai Historical Park, Wat Mahathat, Wat Si Chum; cycle to the ruins, stays are garden resorts · New Town — by the Yom River, near markets and restaurants, value guesthouses, about 15–20 minutes by songthaew to the park · One more special location is Sawankhalok, next to Sukhothai Airport, ideal if you're flying in/out and want a stay in the rice fields.

entries.name: Thai Thai Sukhothai Resort
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Old Town · cycle to the Historical Park
entries.addr: Chedi Thong Rd, Mueang Kao, Mueang Sukhothai
entries.storyHtml: The top score in this guide at 9.6 — Thai Thai is a garden-bungalow resort in the Old Town that guests love for both the staff and the atmosphere, from 211 reviews. Reviewers repeatedly praise the friendly, helpful staff, the generous fresh breakfast, and the pool to cool off in after a day at the ruins. It's an easy cycle to the Historical Park, and at a starting rate of just ฿900 it earns guest scores well above its price.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Pick a Superior Double Bungalow for a garden-view balcony — some in-building rooms are smaller. Bring mosquito repellent, as the garden gets a few at certain times.
pros: Highest guest score in the guide, 9.6 from 211 reviews
Friendly, attentive staff praised across many reviews
Garden bungalows with a pool to cool off in
Old Town location, cyclable to the Historical Park
cons: Some in-building rooms are smaller than the bungalows — check the type
On a quiet lane where places nearby close early — bring late-night snacks

entries.name: Sriwilai Sukhothai Resort & Spa
entries.badge: 💎 Top luxury in the Old Town
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Old Town · near the Historical Park
tags: 🚲 Tuk-tuk shuttle to the Old Town
entries.storyHtml: Sriwilai is the top luxury resort in the Sukhothai Old Town, scoring 9.0. The draw is its Sukhothai-Lanna design, leafy gardens and rice paddies, and an infinity pool with rice-field views that guests photograph endlessly. Rooms are spacious with private balconies looking out over the fields, and a tuk-tuk shuttle runs into the Historical Park. It suits couples and anyone who wants a genuine, restful stay in the World Heritage setting.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Pick a Deluxe Room with a rice-field-view balcony if your budget allows — the morning view is worth it. Book the airport transfer ahead, as taxis are hard to flag in the Old Town.
pros: Close to the Historical Park, cyclable to the ruins
Sukhothai-Lanna design with leafy gardens and rice fields
Infinity pool with rice-field views, varied breakfast
Tuk-tuk shuttle into the Old Town, helpful staff
cons: On-site prices run high — spa, some meals and the airport transfer
Open since 2016, so some rooms show a little wear

entries.name: Legendha Sukhothai Resort
entries.badge: 🏘️ Thai village next to the ruins
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Old Town · backs onto Wat Chang Lom
tags: 🛕 Next to Wat Chang Lom chedi
entries.storyHtml: Legendha is the best-value 4-star in the Old Town, a Thai-village-style boutique resort, scoring 9.1 from 99 reviews. The selling points are teak bungalows in leafy gardens and a location that backs right onto the Wat Chang Lom chedi — you can walk out and photograph it. It's an easy cycle to the Historical Park, and there's a pool with a kids' pool for families. At a starting rate of just ฿1,500, the location and atmosphere are great value.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Go for Deluxe Balcony or higher, as the Superior rooms are smaller. Walk out to photograph the Wat Chang Lom chedi behind the resort in the late-afternoon light.
pros: Old Town location backing onto the Wat Chang Lom chedi
Teak bungalows in a garden, charming Thai-village feel
Pool with a kids' pool, good for families
Great value for a boutique resort in this location
cons: Renovated around 2013, so parts show their age
Superior rooms are smaller — choose Deluxe or higher

entries.name: Sukhothai Heritage Resort
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Sawankhalok · next to the airport, in the rice fields
tags: ✈️ Next to the airport, free shuttle
entries.storyHtml: Sukhothai Heritage is a Sukhothai-style design resort right beside Sukhothai Airport, set quietly in the rice fields, scoring 8.8. The highlights are its photogenic design, two swimming pools, free bicycles and a free airport shuttle — ideal if you're flying in or out of Sukhothai. The trade-off is that it sits about 40–45 minutes from the Historical Park, so it suits a restful stay or a night either side of a flight more than a base for exploring the Old Town.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Great for your first or last night tied to a flight — use the free airport shuttle. If you plan to explore the Old Town, allow travel time or rent a car.
pros: Beside Sukhothai Airport with a free shuttle, very handy if flying in
Photogenic Sukhothai-style design throughout
Two outdoor pools and free bikes to ride through the fields
Quiet in the rice fields, good for genuine relaxation
cons: About 40–45 minutes from the Historical Park — not ideal as an Old Town base
Far from outside restaurants — dinner relies on the resort's dining

entries.name: Phiphu Art and Gallery Boutique
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Old Town · 15-min walk to the park
entries.storyHtml: Phiphu is an Old Town boutique B&B that earns a high 9.0 guest score at a starting rate of just ฿950, from 120 reviews. The rooms are spacious and clean with a big fridge and a roomy bathroom, decorated with artwork so it feels like staying at a local's home. It's a 15-minute walk to the Historical Park, with free bikes to borrow and free parking, and warm hosts. It suits travellers here mainly for the ruins who want a value stay.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ideal if the ruins are your main focus — borrow a free bike for an early-morning ride. Have a translation app handy, as staff speak limited English.
pros: High 9.0 guest score at a starting rate of just ฿950
Spacious, clean rooms with a big fridge and roomy bathroom
15-minute walk to the park, with free bikes
Free parking; warm, attentive hosts
cons: Staff speak limited English — a translation app helps
A small B&B — no pool or full hotel facilities

entries.name: TR Guesthouse
entries.mrtTag: 📍 New Town · near the Yom River, walk to the market
entries.addr: 27/5 Pravet Nakorn Rd, Mueang Sukhothai (New Town)
entries.storyHtml: TR Guesthouse is the most-reviewed stay in this guide — over 520 reviews, scoring 8.8. The strength is its central New Town location, walkable to restaurants and the market, with friendly hosts who arrange transport and motorbike rentals. There are both air-conditioned in-building rooms and quieter, more private garden bungalows; rooms are clean with comfortable beds. At a starting rate of just ฿600 it suits backpackers and budget couples who want to be in the New Town.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Pick a Garden Bungalow for privacy and a garden-view balcony, and rent a motorbike here to ride out to the Old Town yourself.
pros: Most reviewed in the guide, 520 reviews scoring 8.8
Central New Town location, walkable to restaurants and the market
Friendly hosts; motorbike rental and laundry on site
Clean rooms, comfortable beds, great value
cons: Simple facilities — no pool or gym
Breakfast isn't included in every rate (can be added)

entries.name: At Home Sukhothai
entries.mrtTag: 📍 New Town · near the Yom River, wooden house in a garden
tags: 🏡 Wooden house in a garden by a lotus pond
entries.addr: 184/1 Wichian Chamnong Rd, Mueang Sukhothai (New Town)
entries.storyHtml: At Home is the cheapest stay in this guide, from just ฿500, but with the charm of a wooden house in a garden, scoring 8.8 from 213 reviews. The draw is a generous, tasty breakfast served in the garden by a lotus pond, with lounge corners and hammocks to relax in, plus hosts who arrange transport and recommend places to visit. There are fan rooms, air-con rooms and garden bungalows — good for backpackers and budget couples who want atmosphere over a generic in-building guesthouse.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Choose an Air-Con Room or higher in the hot season, and bring mosquito repellent — it's a wooden house in a garden. It's about 10–12 km from the park, so take a songthaew or rent transport.
pros: Cheapest in the guide, from ฿500
Charming wooden house in a garden by a lotus pond
Generous, tasty breakfast served in the garden
Friendly hosts who arrange transport and tips
cons: A wooden garden house — some rooms get mosquitoes; bring repellent
About 10–12 km from the Historical Park — needs a songthaew or rental

entries.name: Tharaburi Resort
entries.badge: 🌿 Garden boutique in the Old Town
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Old Town · near the Historical Park
tags: 🛁 Individually decorated rooms, some with tubs
entries.addr: 321/3 Moo 3, Mueang Kao-Na Pho Rd, Mueang Kao, Mueang Sukhothai
entries.storyHtml: Tharaburi is a garden boutique resort in the Old Town that trades on the individuality of each room, scoring 8.7. The rooms are all decorated differently — some with bathtubs — set in a quiet, leafy garden, with friendly staff who arrange tours and drivers. Breakfast is cooked fresh and can be adjusted to request. It's close to the Old Town ruins with free bikes to borrow, and works out cheaper than the luxury resorts in the same area.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask to see room photos before booking, as each is decorated differently, and pick the Grand Deluxe if you want a separate tub and shower.
pros: Individually decorated rooms with character, in a leafy garden
Friendly staff who arrange tours and drivers
Fresh breakfast, adjustable to request, Thai and Western
Close to the Old Town ruins with free bikes
cons: Some furniture and fittings look older than newer resorts
No 24-hour front desk, and taxis are hard to flag in the quiet Old Town

entries.name: Baan Georges Hotel
entries.mrtTag: 📍 New Town · by the Yom River, walk to street food
tags: 🚶 Walk to New Town street food
entries.addr: 28/54 Soi Chaiwannasut, Jarodvithithong Rd, Mueang Sukhothai (New Town)
entries.storyHtml: Baan Georges is a tiny 8-room boutique pool hotel in the New Town that trades on a warm, stay-with-a-friend feel, scoring 8.7 from 263 reviews. The standout many reviews mention is the rooftop breakfast with fresh-baked bread and brewed coffee, plus hosts who welcome you like family. There's a pool to cool off in — rare at this price — and it's a few minutes' walk to restaurants and street food in the New Town, about 15 minutes by car from the park.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: With only 8 rooms it fills fast in high season, so book ahead. The entrance is down a lane — watch out for the soi dogs if you're walking back late.
pros: Rooftop breakfast with fresh-baked bread and coffee, widely praised
Small 8-room hotel with a warm, stay-with-a-friend feel
A pool to cool off in — rare at this price
A few minutes' walk to New Town restaurants and street food
cons: Down a deep lane with several soi dogs, some bark at night
About 15 minutes by car from the Historical Park

entries.name: Le Charme Sukhothai Resort
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Old Town · near the Historical Park
entries.addr: 9/9 Na Pho-Khiri Mat Rd, Mueang Kao, Mueang Sukhothai
entries.storyHtml: Le Charme is a boutique resort set in a tropical garden around a lotus pond, suited to a quiet, restful stay in the Old Town, scoring 8.6. The draw is the leafy garden around the lotus pond, spacious clean rooms with private balconies facing the pond or garden, and an outdoor saltwater pool. It's close to the Old Town ruins, cyclable for sightseeing, with friendly staff and fresh breakfast — good for those wanting a garden resort at a moderate price in the World Heritage area.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for a room facing the lotus pond for the better outlook, and arrange transport — nights are very quiet with few restaurants nearby.
pros: Tropical garden around a lotus pond, quiet and restful
Spacious, clean rooms with pond- or garden-view balconies
Outdoor saltwater pool, close to the ruins
Friendly staff, fresh breakfast, cyclable for sightseeing
cons: Classic-style decor, some parts starting to look dated
The Old Town is very quiet at night with few outside restaurants — arrange transport

advice.bodyHtml: → At Home Sukhothai ฿500, a wooden house in a garden by a lotus pond · or TR Guesthouse ฿600, the most-reviewed guesthouse in the New Town

advice.head: Here for the ruins, want to stay in the Old Town
advice.bodyHtml: → Thai Thai Sukhothai Resort ฿900, garden bungalows scoring 9.6 · or Phiphu Art and Gallery ฿950, an art boutique a 15-min walk from the park

advice.head: A restful couples' trip with atmosphere
advice.bodyHtml: → Sriwilai Sukhothai Resort & Spa ฿3,200, a luxury resort with rice-field views · or Legendha Sukhothai Resort ฿1,500, a Thai village next to the Wat Chang Lom chedi

advice.head: Travelling as a family with kids
advice.bodyHtml: → Legendha Sukhothai Resort ฿1,500, with a kids' pool and a Two Bedroom Villa · or Le Charme Sukhothai Resort ฿1,800, a Family Suite in a lotus-pond garden

faqTitle: FAQ — Common traveller questions about Sukhothai hotels

faq.q: ❓ Should I stay in the Old Town or New Town in Sukhothai?
faq.a: The Old Town suits trips focused on the Historical Park — stays are garden resorts and you can cycle to the ruins straight from your hotel (Thai Thai, Sriwilai, Legendha, Phiphu, Tharaburi, Le Charme), but there are few dinner options at night. The New Town is about 12 km away by the Yom River, walkable to markets and restaurants with value stays (TR Guesthouse, At Home, Baan Georges), 15–20 minutes by songthaew to the park.

faq.q: ❓ How much do Sukhothai hotels cost?
faq.a: Prices start very low: guesthouses and bungalows from around ฿500–950 a night · boutique resorts and 4-star around ฿1,500–2,900 · 5-star luxury resorts from ฿3,200 up (villas to around ฿6,800). All are indicative starting rates from standard rooms; during the Loy Krathong festival (Nov) they can run higher and fill fast.

faq.q: ❓ How far ahead should I book a Sukhothai hotel?
faq.a: For normal weekdays, 1–2 weeks ahead is enough. But during the Loy Krathong / Light & Candle Festival (November), Sukhothai's biggest event, good rooms in the Old Town fill very fast — book 1–2 months ahead or more.

faq.q: ❓ How do I get around Sukhothai without a car?
faq.a: In the Old Town most stays offer free bicycles, easy for riding around the Historical Park. If you stay in the New Town, a songthaew into the park takes about 15–20 minutes, or rent a motorbike/bicycle from your guesthouse. Taxis are hard to flag in the Old Town — plan ahead or use a resort shuttle.

faq.q: ❓ Where should I stay to visit the Sukhothai Historical Park?
faq.a: Staying in the Old Town is easiest, as you can cycle to the park from your hotel. Value picks are Thai Thai (฿900) and Phiphu (฿950) · for a garden resort, Legendha (฿1,500) or Le Charme (฿1,800) · with a bigger budget for luxury, Sriwilai (฿3,200) with rice-field views.

faq.q: ❓ Where should I stay if I fly into Sukhothai Airport?
faq.a: If you're flying in/out and want to be near the airport, Sukhothai Heritage Resort sits beside Sukhothai Airport in Sawankhalok with a free shuttle, ideal for a night tied to a flight. But it's about 40–45 minutes from the Historical Park — to focus on the Old Town, stay in the Old Town area instead.
